newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba says investigating Sri Lanka boat incident.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says investigating Sri Lanka boat incident.

text.p: Cuba said on Tuesday it was investigating an incident in which a Cuban-crewed, Cypriot-flagged vessel was attacked by Sri Lankan armed forces helicopters last weekend.

The ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma said that according to press reports and the Sri Lankan Defence Ministry statement, "this serious incident" occurred because Sri Lankan armed forces confused the boat, the Caribbean Queen, with a vessel allegedly illegally carrying arms for Tamil anti-government rebels.
In Colombo, the Sri Lankan navy said on Tuesday it would soon free the Caribbean Queen after it had been searched for weapons and none had been found.

The 1,674-tonne ship, with a crew of 28 Cubans, was seized by navy patrol boats on Sunday after it ignored repeated radio calls and warning shots from military aircraft and started manoeuvres to escape, the Defence Ministry said.
"We searched the ship after she was detained because she was making suspicious movements," a navy spokesman told Reuters. "Nothing suspicious was found and we're going to release her."
Granma said the Cuban ambassador in Sri Lanka had gone to the northern port of Trincomalee, where the Caribbean Queen was docked, to check the ship and its crew.

Granma said Cuban authorities were informed of the incident on Sunday by the ship's captain, Miguel Amaral Ravelo, who said his vessel was attacked that afternoon by two Sri Lankan helicopters 27.5 miles from the Sri Lankan coast in international waters.
